body:
Today's scan turned up zero cross-platform arbitrage opportunities — a quiet day. The scanner checks Kalshi's gold settlement ladder against Polymarket's touch and direction markets and found no combination of legs where the net edge, after fees and available book depth, was positive. That's the normal state of affairs; genuine mispricings between these platforms are rare and don't last long when they appear.

On pricing, Kalshi's gold above $X on September 30, 2026 ladder implies the market sees spot trading roughly in the $4,300–$4,400 zone right now: the $4,290.99 strike still has a 60/70 yes bid/ask, while $4,370.99 sits near 56/57, roughly where the crowd is split on whether settlement lands above or below. One thing worth flagging for anyone staring at the raw table: the $4,330.99 strike shows a lower yes-bid (0.53) than the higher $4,370.99 strike (0.56), which is backwards — a higher price target should be cheaper, not pricier, to bet on. That's not a real arbitrage; it's a symptom of thin trading (26 contracts of 24-hour volume on the $4,330.99 line versus 156 on the $4,370.99 one), so the quote is stale rather than mispriced in any tradable sense.

Kalshi's contracts here are settlement markets — they pay out based on a single price snapshot at expiry — while Polymarket's gold markets are a mix of touch (did price ever hit a level intramonth) and daily up/down bets, which resolve on different rules entirely. That structural difference is the most common reason a same-looking strike shows different prices across the two venues, and it's worth keeping in mind before reading any gap as free money. Separately, Polymarket's brand-new Up or Down on September 9 contract shows a 0.03/0.97 bid-ask with no recorded volume yet — a wide-open, unseasoned book rather than a signal of anything.
headline: No cross-platform gold arbitrage found; Kalshi ladder implies spot near $4,300-$4,400
